title: Adjectives and comparison
goal: Describe things and compare them — while accepting one Estonian habit with no English equivalent at all: **adjectives change form along with their noun**.
bekal: name the most common colors and qualities
make an adjective copy the form of its noun

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Eesti ja Indoneesia
dialogs.intro: On the balcony of Kerli's apartment, late afternoon. The conversation turns to comparing the two countries.

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.text: Kumb linn on suurem, Bandung või Jakarta?
lines.id: Which city is bigger, Bandung or Jakarta?
lines.literal: which-of-two city is-it bigger, Bandung or Jakarta?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Jakarta, muidugi. See on palju suurem.
lines.id: Jakarta, of course. It's much bigger.
lines.literal: Jakarta, of-course. it is-it much bigger.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Umbes kümme miljonit. Rohkem kui kogu Eesti.
lines.id: About ten million. More than all of Estonia.
lines.literal: about ten million-part. more than whole Estonia.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Ei, ma olen aus. Vanalinn on väga ilus.
lines.id: No, I'm being honest. The old town is very beautiful.
lines.literal: no, I am-I honest. old-town is-it very beautiful.

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.text: Aitäh. Ja mis on Eestis kõige raskem?
lines.id: Thanks. And what's the hardest thing in Estonia?
lines.literal: thanks. and what is-it Estonia-in most difficult?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Ma tean seda nüüd. Aga suvi on parim.
lines.id: I know that now. But summer is the best.
lines.literal: I know-I it-part now. but summer is-it best.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Muidugi. Igal keelel on oma erandid.
lines.id: Of course. Every language has its own exceptions.
lines.literal: of-course. every language-on are own exceptions.

notes: **Kumb** means "which one" when there are **two** choices. With more than two, use *milline*: *Milline raamat on kõige parem?* It's like English "which of the two" versus "which".
**Suurem, ilusam, külmem, pimedam** — all adjective + **-m**. One letter does the job of English "-er" or "more". Handy, and it becomes comfortable quickly.
**Kui** here means "than": *suurem kui Tartu*. Remember that *kui* also means "how" (unit 2) and "if/when". Three jobs, one word, and context always tells them apart.

⚠️ **Parim, not "heam".** *Hea* (good) is irregular: *hea – parem – parim*. It's the exception you'll meet most often, and it's the exact counterpart of English *good – better – best* — so the idea should already feel familiar.

grammars.title: ⚠️ The adjective copies its noun
body: In English, "big" stays "big" wherever it stands: a big house, in a big house, from a big house. In Estonian, the adjective changes form every time its noun does.
after: Notice that **both words take the same ending** in almost every row. Once you know the form of the noun, the adjective follows — so this isn't a second table to memorize, just the old table used twice.
You've already met this rule several times without its name: *rohelist teed* in unit 5, *midagi head* in unit 12, *millist raamatut* in unit 13. All of them are adjectives copying their noun.
⚠️ If you forget to change the adjective, Estonians still understand you completely. It's a mistake that marks you as a learner, not one that breaks understanding. Don't let it slow your speech.

grammars.title: Comparing — -m and kõige
body: Two degrees, two ways to form them. Both attach to the **genitive**, not the nominative.
after: **Kõige** means "most" and goes in front of the comparative form. There's also a short form ending in *-im* (*suurim*, *parim*, *ilusaim*), but it sounds more written; in conversation, *kõige* is more common and always safe.
To say "as ... as", use *sama ... kui*: *Ta on sama pikk kui mina.* (He/she is as tall as me.)
The last four rows are irregular and frequent. Three of them match English (*good–better–best*, *bad–worse*, *much–more*), so they come almost for free.

blocks.text: The last two rows show a pattern that works for every color: **hele-** = light, **tume-** = dark. *Heleroheline* (light green), *tumepunane* (dark red). Two prefixes, twenty new colors.
⚠️ The Estonian flag is *sinimustvalge* — "blue-black-white", written as one word. When you hear it, it almost always means the flag, not three colors that happen to sit side by side.

⚠️ Notice *must* appears twice: it means both **black** and **dirty**. Likewise *kerge* means light and easy, and *raske* means heavy and hard — pairings English speakers will recognize from "a light task" and "a heavy workload".

blocks.title: Comparing — ready-made sentences
items: *Tallinn on suurem kui Tartu.* — Tallinn is bigger than Tartu.
*See on palju odavam.* — This is much cheaper.
*Kumb on parem?* — Which one is better?
*See on kõige parem.* — This one is the best.
